mainTopic: When a more frequent (תדיר) item and a holier (מקודש) item clash, which comes first? The גמרא tries five proofs that תדיר wins, and rejects each one.
overview: This amud deals with which קרבן or מצוה comes first. First the גמרא tries to prove that a frequent item (תדיר) beats a holier one (מקודש), using the order of offerings, the blessings of קידוש, and davening מנחה before מוסף. Each proof is rejected the same way: the holiness of the day spreads to the frequent item too, so the two are really equal. A proof the other way, from שלמים and חטאת, is rejected by רבא: שלמים are only common (מצוי), not truly frequent (תדיר). Next the גמרא asks what happens if the less frequent offering was slaughtered first. Every proof is pushed off, because each one turns out to be a case where both things were ready together. The גמרא then explains why כהנים may eat קדשים prepared any way they like, 'like kings.' Finally a new משנה opens: רבי שמעון explains where oil handed out in the עזרה or burned on the מזבח comes from, and רבי טרפון holds that oil may be donated.

steps.title: Daily offerings go first even though the additional offerings seem holier
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the proof from the משנה that תמידין come before מוספין: the frequent offering goes first even though the מוספין seem holier.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is so even though the additional offerings are holier!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof it began on the previous daf. The proof is that תמידין come before מוספין even though the מוספין seem holier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מוספין are brought only because of the special holiness of שבת, so they look like the 'holier' item. The תמיד is brought every day, so it is the 'frequent' item. If the תמיד still goes first, then תדיר seems to beat מקודש.

keyTerms.meaning: The additional offerings brought on שבת, ראש חודש, and holidays
The daily offerings brought every morning and afternoon

phrases.english: And even though the additional offerings are holier!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a proof that began before this section, from the משנה's rule that תמידין come before מוספין.
steps.raayaObject: That תדיר takes precedence over מקודש
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's rule that תמידין come before מוספין, even though the מוספין seem holier

steps.title: שבת makes the daily offerings holy too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the holiness of שבת affects the תמידין of that day too, so both offerings are equally holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you really think שבת affects only the additional offerings and not the daily offerings?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It says the holiness of שבת also spreads to the daily offerings brought on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תמיד brought on שבת is just as holy as the מוסף, then there is no 'holier' side here at all. The only difference left is frequency, so of course the תמיד goes first. That tells us nothing about a real clash between תדיר and מקודש.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you really think...? (a question that rejects an idea)
It had an effect (here: it added holiness)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the מוספין are less holy. It is saying the תמידין of שבת are raised to the same level, so the two are equal.

phrases.english: Is that to say that Shabbat has an effect on the additional offerings,
but has no effect on the daily offerings?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from תמידין and מוספין
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the מוספין are holier, but the holiness of שבת raises the תמידין of that day equally.

steps.title: The מוספין of שבת come before those of ראש חודש
steps.stepSummary: A second proof from the משנה: מוספי שבת come before מוספי ראש חודש because they are more frequent.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: the additional offerings of שבת come before the additional offerings of ראש חודש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof from the same משנה. When שבת and ראש חודש fall on the same day, the שבת offerings go first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבת comes every week and ראש חודש comes once a month, so שבת is the more frequent one. The proof assumes the ראש חודש offerings are 'holier' on that day because ראש חודש adds holiness to its own offerings. If שבת still goes first, then תדיר wins.

keyTerms.meaning: The additional offerings of the new month

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: מוּסְפֵי שַׁבָּת קוֹדְמִין לְמוּסְפֵי רֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ!
phrases.english: The additional offerings of Shabbat come before the additional offerings of Rosh Chodesh!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מוּסְפֵי שַׁבָּת קוֹדְמִין לְמוּסְפֵי רֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, the גמרא tries a new one.
steps.raayaObject: That תדיר takes precedence over מקודש
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's rule that מוספי שבת come before מוספי ראש חודש

steps.title: ראש חודש makes the שבת offerings holy too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects this proof too: ראש חודש adds holiness to the שבת offerings of that day as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you really think ראש חודש affects only its own additional offerings and not the additional offerings of שבת?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same answer again. The holiness of ראש חודש also spreads to the שבת offerings brought that day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since both sets of offerings get the holiness of ראש חודש, they are equally holy. The only difference is that שבת is more frequent, so this is not a real clash between תדיר and מקודש.

phrases.aramaic: אַטּוּ רֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ לְמוּסָפִין דִּידֵיהּ אַהֲנִי,
phrases.english: Is that to say that Rosh Chodesh has an effect on its own additional offerings,
but has no effect on the additional offerings of Shabbat?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ רֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ לְמוּסָפִין דִּידֵיהּ אַהֲנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 3 the same way step 2 rejected step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from מוספי שבת and מוספי ראש חודש
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The holiness of ראש חודש raises the שבת offerings of that day too, so neither side is holier.

steps.title: ראש חודש offerings come before ראש השנה offerings
steps.stepSummary: A third proof: מוספי ראש חודש come before מוספי ראש השנה, even though ראש השנה is holier.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: the additional offerings of ראש חודש come before the additional offerings of ראש השנה, even though ראש השנה is holier!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third proof from the משנה. Here the other day, ראש השנה, is openly called holier, and still the more frequent ראש חודש offerings go first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ראש השנה is also ראש חודש of תשרי, so both sets of offerings are brought that day. ראש חודש comes every month and ראש השנה once a year. This proof seems stronger, because the גמרא says outright that ראש השנה is holier.

keyTerms.meaning: The new year, which is also the first of the month of תשרי

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: מוּסְפֵי רֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ קוֹדְמִין
phrases.english: Come and hear: The additional offerings of Rosh Chodesh come before
the additional offerings of Rosh Hashanah.
phrases.notes: ראש השנה is also the first of the month, so both sets of offerings are brought on the same day.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה קַדִּשָׁה!
phrases.english: Even though Rosh Hashanah is holier!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מוּסְפֵי רֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ קוֹדְמִין לְמוּסְפֵי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the second proof was rejected, the גמרא tries a third.
steps.raayaObject: That תדיר takes precedence over מקודש
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's rule that מוספי ראש חודש come before מוספי ראש השנה

steps.title: ראש השנה makes the ראש חודש offerings holy too
steps.stepSummary: Rejected again: the holiness of ראש השנה also spreads to the ראש חודש offerings brought that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you really think ראש השנה affects only its own additional offerings and not the additional offerings of ראש חודש?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer a third time. ראש השנה raises the holiness of the ראש חודש offerings brought on that day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though ראש השנה itself is a holier day, its holiness covers every offering brought on it. So the two sets of offerings are equally holy, and frequency decides the order.

keyTerms.meaning: It has an effect (another form of אַהֲנַאי)

phrases.aramaic: אַטּוּ רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לְמוּסְפֵי דִּידֵיהּ אַהֲנִי,
phrases.english: Is that to say that Rosh Hashanah has an effect on its own additional offerings,
but has no effect on the additional offerings of Rosh Chodesh?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לְמוּסְפֵי דִּידֵיהּ אַהֲנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 5 with the same pattern.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from מוספי ראש חודש and מוספי ראש השנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The holiness of ראש השנה also covers the ראש חודש offerings of that day, so the two are equal.

steps.title: The wine blessing comes before the blessing of the day in קידוש
steps.stepSummary: A fourth proof, from קידוש: the ברכת היין is said first because it is frequent, even though ברכת היום is holier.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: another reason. The blessing on wine is frequent and the blessing of the day is not frequent, and when frequent and not frequent meet, the frequent comes first. This is so even though the blessing of the day is holier!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from offerings to blessings. In קידוש, the blessing on the wine is said before the blessing about the day, because the wine blessing is said far more often.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the source states the rule outright: תדיר comes first. The blessing of the day exists only because of the holiness of שבת, so it looks like the holier item. If the frequent wine blessing still comes first, תדיר seems to beat מקודש.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing on wine (בורא פרי הגפן)
The blessing about the holiness of the day, said in קידוש

phrases.english: Come and hear: Another reason –
phrases.notes: This is the second reason בית הלל give for saying the wine blessing first in קידוש.

phrases.english: the blessing on wine is frequent
and the blessing of the day is not frequent,
and between frequent and not frequent, the frequent comes first.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּבִרְכַּת הַיּוֹם קַדִּישָׁה!
phrases.english: Even though the blessing of the day is holier!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: דָּבָר אַחֵר – בִּרְכַּת הַיַּיִן תְּדִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After three proofs from offerings were rejected, the גמרא tries a proof from the order of blessings in קידוש.
steps.raayaObject: That תדיר takes precedence over מקודש
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second reason of בית הלל for the order of קידוש: תדיר קודם

steps.title: שבת makes the wine blessing holy too
steps.stepSummary: Rejected: the holiness of שבת also affects the wine blessing said in קידוש, so the two blessings are equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you really think שבת affects only the blessing of the day and not the blessing on the wine?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the fourth proof the same way it answered the others. The holiness of שבת also covers the wine blessing said as part of קידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wine blessing in קידוש is part of honoring שבת, so it shares the day's holiness. Both blessings are equally holy, and frequency alone decides which comes first. So the question of תדיר against a truly holier item is still open.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessings said over wine to declare the holiness of שבת or יום טוב

steps.whatToRemember: Every proof here fails for the same reason. The special holiness of the day spreads to everything done on that day, including the frequent item. So these cases are only 'frequent vs. equal', never 'frequent vs. holier'.

phrases.english: Is that to say that Shabbat has an effect on the blessing of the day,
but has no effect on the blessing on the wine?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 7 using the same pattern as steps 2, 4, and 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the order of blessings in קידוש
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The holiness of שבת also covers the wine blessing of קידוש, so the blessing of the day is not truly holier.

steps.title: Proof from praying מנחה before מוסף
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that a person prays מנחה first and then מוסף. Since מנחה is more frequent and מוסף is holier, this seems to prove that תדיר comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יוחנן said the הלכה is that a person prays מנחה first, and only afterward מוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a fifth proof that the frequent מצוה comes before the holier one, this time from the order of prayers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנחה is said every day, so it is תדיר. מוסף is said only on special days like שבת, so it seems more holy. If רבי יוחנן puts מנחה first, it looks like תדיר beats מקודש.

keyTerms.meaning: The afternoon prayer, said every day
The additional prayer, said only on שבת, יום טוב and ראש חודש

phrases.english: Come and hear, as Rabbi Yochanan says:
The halacha is: a person prays the afternoon prayer,
and afterward the additional prayer!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the קידוש proof was rejected, the גמרא tries a new proof from prayer order.
steps.raayaObject: That תדיר takes precedence over מקודש
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling that מנחה is prayed before מוסף

steps.title: שבת makes מנחה holy too
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. שבת gives holiness to the מנחה prayer of that day as well, so both prayers are equally holy and only frequency decides.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you really think שבת adds holiness to מוסף but not to מנחה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from רבי יוחנן, using the same kind of answer it gave to the earlier proofs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנחה said on שבת is a שבת prayer too, so it shares שבת's holiness. With holiness equal on both sides, frequency breaks the tie. That tells us nothing about a real clash between תדיר and מקודש.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? It opens a question that means 'surely not!'

phrases.english: Is that to say that Shabbat has an effect on the additional prayer,
but on the afternoon prayer it has no effect?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from prayer order
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed מוסף is holier than מנחה. In fact שבת makes both holy, so the case is not a clash between תדיר and מקודש.

steps.title: Proof from חטאת and אשם coming before שלמים
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says שלמים left from yesterday come before today's חטאת or אשם. This implies that if both are from today, חטאת and אשם come first, even though שלמים are more frequent. That would mean מקודש beats תדיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if there are שלמים from yesterday and a חטאת or אשם from today, the שלמים from yesterday come first. So if both are from today, the חטאת and אשם come first, even though שלמים are more frequent!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new proof, and this time it points the other way: the holier offering comes before the more frequent one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חטאת and אשם are קדשי קדשים, the holiest kind of offering. שלמים are lighter in holiness but brought much more often. The inference from the משנה puts the holier offerings first, which suggests that מקודש wins over תדיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offering and guilt offering, both of higher holiness
This one and that one, meaning both
This implies: introduces an inference from the text

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלָמִים שֶׁל אֶמֶשׁ, חַטָּאת וְאָשָׁם שֶׁל יוֹם –
phrases.english: A peace offering from yesterday, and a sin offering or guilt offering from today:
the peace offering from yesterday comes first.
This implies that if both are from today,
the sin offering and guilt offering come first,
even though peace offerings are more frequent!

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the direction. The earlier proofs tried to show that תדיר comes first. This one tries to show the opposite, that the holier offering comes first.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the prayer proof, the גמרא brings a proof for the opposite side.
steps.raayaObject: That מקודש takes precedence over תדיר
steps.raayaSupportSource: An inference from the משנה about שלמים של אמש and חטאת and אשם of today

steps.title: רבא: common is not the same as frequent
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the proof. שלמים are only מצוי, meaning people happen to bring them often, but there is no fixed requirement to bring them regularly. Our question is only about something that is truly תדיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You are talking about something common?! Our question is about something frequent. We are not asking about something that is merely common.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down the proof from שלמים by drawing a line between 'frequent' and 'common'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תדיר means a מצוה with a regular, built-in schedule. שלמים are brought often only because many people choose to bring them, so they are just מצוי. The משנה therefore tells us nothing about a true clash between תדיר and מקודש.

keyTerms.meaning: Common: happens often, but without a fixed requirement
Frequent: comes on a regular, fixed schedule
We are asking about it, or it is our question

phrases.english: Rava said: Are you speaking of something common?!
Something frequent is what we are asking about;
something common we are not asking about.

steps.whyThisMatters: This introduces a new idea: being 'frequent' (תדיר) is not the same as being 'common' (מצוי).
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from שלמים versus חטאת and אשם
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שלמים are only מצוי (common), not תדיר (frequent), so the case is not a real clash between תדיר and מקודש.

steps.title: רב הונא בר יהודה: a ברייתא calls a common מצוה frequent
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר יהודה challenges רבא's line between common and frequent. A ברייתא calls מילה 'frequent' compared to פסח, even though מילה has no fixed schedule and is only common.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה said to רבא: Is common not the same as frequent? But a ברייתא teaches: 'I should exclude פסח, which is not frequent, but not exclude מילה, which is frequent!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר יהודה attacks רבא's answer by showing a source that seems to treat 'common' as 'frequent'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מילה happens whenever a boy is born, so it has no fixed calendar, just like שלמים. Yet the ברייתא calls it תדיר. That suggests a מצוה that is merely common still counts as תדיר, which would bring back the proof from שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: The קרבן פסח, brought once a year

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yehuda said to Rava:
Is that to say that something common is not frequent?!
But isn't it taught in a baraita:
I should exclude the Pesach offering, which is not frequent,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אוֹצִיא אֶת הַמִּילָה שֶׁהִיא תְּדִירָה!
phrases.english: and I should not exclude circumcision, which is frequent!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה לְרָבָא: אַטּוּ מָצוּי לָאו תָּדִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's line between מצוי and תדיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא calls מילה תדיר even though it is only common and has no fixed schedule. So common things do count as תדיר, and שלמים should count as תדיר too.

steps.title: Frequent here means rich in מצוות
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the ברייתא calls מילה 'frequent' because it has many מצוות connected to it. It does not mean frequent in timing.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'frequent' mean there? Frequent in מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his line between מצוי and תדיר. He says the word 'frequent' in the ברייתא about מילה means something different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא בר יהודה argued that a ברייתא calls מילה תדיר even though it has no fixed schedule. רבא answers that 'frequent' there is about how many מצוות are tied to מילה, not about how often it happens. So the ברייתא does not prove that 'common' counts as תדיר.

keyTerms.meaning: frequent in מצוות, meaning it has many מצוות connected to it

phrases.english: What does 'frequent' mean?
phrases.notes: This is רבא's answer to the ברייתא about מילה from step 13.

phrases.english: Frequent in מצוות.
phrases.notes: He means מילה has many מצוות tied to it. So the word isn't about a regular schedule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a word in the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא calls מילה תדיר even though it is only common, so common counts as תדיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Frequent' there means many מצוות, so it says nothing about common versus frequent.

steps.title: Compared to פסח, מילה is like frequent
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: next to פסח, which comes once a year, מילה happens so much more often that it is treated like תדיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: circumcision compared to the פסח offering is like something frequent.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second, different answer to the same challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'frequent' does mean how often, but only in comparison. מילה is so much more common than פסח that it counts as תדיר. שלמים are not that much more common than חטאת, so the משנה in step 11 still does not prove that מקודש beats תדיר.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you want, say; introduces a second answer
the קרבן פסח, brought once a year

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's line still stands: being only common (מצוי) is not the same as truly frequent (תדיר). So the משנה about שלמים does not decide between תדיר and מקודש.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
Circumcision compared to the פסח offering
is like something frequent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second answer to the same קשיא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מילה is called תדיר just because it is common.
steps.terutzMaskana: מילה is only called תדיר because it is far more frequent than פסח. That comparison does not carry over to שלמים and חטאת.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The proof from the משנה of שלמים stays rejected.

steps.title: What if the less-frequent offering was slaughtered first?
steps.stepSummary: New question: if the כהן slaughtered the less-frequent offering first, does he keep going with it, or does he hold its blood until the frequent one is offered?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: a frequent offering and an infrequent one, and he went ahead and slaughtered the infrequent one first. What is the law? Do we say that since he slaughtered it, he offers it? Or perhaps he gives it to another כהן who stirs its blood until he offers the frequent one, and then he offers the infrequent one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about precedence. It asks what to do after the order was already broken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know תדיר should go first. The question is whether that rule still applies once the other offering is already slaughtered. One side says finish what you started. The other side says hold the blood so it doesn't spoil, and go back to the right order.

keyTerms.meaning: it was asked of them; opens a question the חכמים were unsure about

phrases.english: They asked:
A frequent offering and an infrequent one,
and he went ahead and slaughtered the infrequent one first — what is the law?
Do we say:
since he slaughtered it, he offers it;
or perhaps, he gives it to another
who stirs its blood
until he offers the frequent one,
and then he offers the infrequent one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about precedence
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the rule that תדיר comes first still apply after the less-frequent offering has already been slaughtered?

steps.title: Proof from yesterday's שלמים and today's חטאת
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא מסורא brings the משנה: yesterday's שלמים come before today's חטאת and אשם. The implication is that today's שלמים, even if already slaughtered, still wait for the חטאת and אשם. So an offering already slaughtered still waits for the one with priority.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא from Sura said: Come and hear: peace offerings from yesterday, and a sin offering and guilt offering from today, the one from yesterday comes before the one from today. This implies that one from today that is like yesterday's, meaning already slaughtered first, does not come first. The sin and guilt offerings come first!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא מסורא tries to answer the new question from the same משנה used in step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Yesterday's שלמים were already slaughtered and are waiting for their blood to be offered. 'Today's that is like yesterday's' means today's שלמים that were also slaughtered first. Even so, the חטאת and אשם go first. In the same way, a slaughtered שאינו תדיר should wait while the תדיר is offered.
steps.confusionAlert: In step 11 this משנה was used about תדיר versus מקודש. Here it is used for a different point: whether an offering that was already slaughtered still has to wait.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא מִסּוּרָא, תָּא שְׁמַע:
phrases.english: Rav Huna from Sura said: Come and hear:
Peace offerings from yesterday,
a sin offering and guilt offering from today –
the one from yesterday comes before the one from today.
This implies that one from today
that is like the one from yesterday –
phrases.notes: Yesterday's שלמים were already slaughtered. So 'like it' means today's שלמים that were also already slaughtered.

phrases.english: and what case is that?
where he slaughtered the peace offerings first –
the sin and guilt offerings come first!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא מִסּוּרָא, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question of step 16
steps.raayaObject: An offering slaughtered out of order still waits for the one that has priority.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about yesterday's שלמים and today's חטאת and אשם, read by inference: today's שלמים, even already slaughtered, wait for the חטאת and אשם.

steps.title: Maybe the משנה is about both offerings already slaughtered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof from the משנה. Maybe the משנה is talking about a case where both the שלמים and the חטאת or אשם were already slaughtered. If only the שלמים was slaughtered, the question still stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps the משנה about yesterday's שלמים and today's חטאת and אשם is talking about a case where both were already slaughtered. But if both were not slaughtered, your question is still open.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 17. It says the משנה may be talking about a narrower case than we assumed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 read the משנה as saying that an offering already slaughtered still waits for the one with priority. The גמרא answers that the משנה may be about a case where both animals' blood is already waiting at the same time. In that case, the משנה is only telling us which blood to put on the מזבח first. It tells us nothing about stopping a slaughtered offering to go slaughter a new one.

keyTerms.meaning: How do you find this case? (in what situation is it true)
You can still ask it; the question remains

phrases.english: Perhaps the peace offering of yesterday
and the sin offering and guilt offering of today
how do you find this case?
where he slaughtered both of them;
but if he did not slaughter both of them –
you can still ask your question.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא שְׁלָמִים דְּאֶמֶשׁ וְחַטָּאת וְאָשָׁם דְּיוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 17
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected; the question from step 16 remains open
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה may be talking about a case where both offerings were already slaughtered, so it does not answer our case

steps.title: Proof from the order of blessings in קידוש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings בית הלל's reason in קידוש: the blessing on wine is frequent and the blessing of the day is not, and frequent comes first. The blessing of the day became an obligation first, yet the wine blessing still goes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come hear: another reason is that the blessing on wine is frequent and the blessing of the day is not frequent. When something frequent meets something not frequent, the frequent one comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new proof for the question from step 16. It uses the order of the blessings in קידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The obligation of the blessing of the day starts as soon as שבת begins, before the wine is even on the table. That is like an offering that was already slaughtered. Still, the wine blessing, which is more frequent, is said first. So the proof suggests that the frequent offering also goes first, even if the less frequent one was already begun.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing on the wine (בורא פרי הגפן)
The blessing about the holiness of the day (in קידוש)

phrases.english: Come and hear: another reason –
phrases.notes: This is בית הלל's second reason for saying the wine blessing first in קידוש.

phrases.english: the blessing on wine is frequent
and the blessing of the day is not frequent,
and between frequent and not frequent –
the frequent one comes first!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 18 rejects the first proof, this brings a new proof
steps.raayaObject: That the frequent one goes first even when the less frequent one's obligation already started
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of בית הלל about the order of the blessings in קידוש

steps.title: In קידוש, both obligations are present together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the קידוש proof. Once the wine is there, both blessings are ready at the same moment. That is like a case where both animals were already slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, since the wine has come, it is like a case where both were slaughtered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof from קידוש. It uses the same idea it used in step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קידוש is only said once there is wine. At that point, both the wine blessing and the blessing of the day are ready together. So קידוש is like two slaughtered offerings that are both waiting, and it does not teach our case of one slaughtered and one not.

keyTerms.meaning: It is like a case where both were slaughtered

phrases.english: Here too, since
(they come) [the wine has come] –
phrases.notes: Read it without the words in round brackets, using the square-bracket words: 'since the wine has come.'

phrases.english: it is like a case where both were slaughtered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 19
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from קידוש is rejected
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In קידוש, both obligations are present together once the wine arrives

steps.title: Proof from davening מנחה before מוסף
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that a person davens מנחה first and then מוסף. This is true even though the obligation of מוסף started earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come hear, as רבי יוחנן said: the halacha is that a person davens מנחה and afterward מוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a third proof for the question from step 16. It uses the order of the תפילות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The obligation of מוסף began in the morning, long before מנחה. That is like an offering that was already slaughtered. Still, מנחה, which is the more frequent prayer, goes first. So this suggests that the frequent offering takes the lead even when the other one was already started.

keyTerms.meaning: The additional prayer (only on שבת, ראש חודש and יום טוב)

phrases.english: Come and hear, as Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halacha is: a person prays the afternoon prayer
and afterward the additional prayer!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 20 rejects the קידוש proof, this brings a new proof
steps.raayaObject: That the frequent one goes first even though the less frequent one's obligation came earlier
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling that מנחה is davened before מוסף

steps.title: Once it is time for מנחה, both prayers are due together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the תפילה proof. When the time of מנחה arrives, both prayers are due at once. So this is again like a case where both animals were already slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, since the time of the מנחה prayer has arrived, it is like a case where both were slaughtered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof from רבי יוחנן. It uses the same answer it gave for קידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's ruling only applies once מנחה time has come. At that moment, both מנחה and מוסף are obligations at the same time. So it is like two offerings that were both already slaughtered, and the question from step 16 stays open.
steps.whatToRemember: All three proofs fail for the same reason. Each one is a case where both obligations are present together, like two animals already slaughtered. None of them tells us what to do when only the less frequent offering was slaughtered.

phrases.english: Here too, since there has arrived
the time of the afternoon prayer –
it is like a case where both were slaughtered.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, כֵּיוָן דְּמָטֵי זְמַן תְּפִלַּת מִנְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 21, using the same reasoning as step 20
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from תפילה is rejected
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Once מנחה time arrives, both prayers are due together

steps.title: Proof from the קרבן פסח slaughtered before the afternoon תמיד
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב אשי brings a משנה from פסחים. A קרבן פסח slaughtered before the תמיד is valid, but its blood waits until the תמיד's blood is sprinkled. So the frequent offering still goes first, even though the פסח was ready first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב אשי said to רבינא: 'If he slaughtered the פסח before midday, it is disqualified, because the פסוק says "in the afternoon." If he slaughtered it before the תמיד, it is valid, and someone should keep stirring its blood until he sprinkles the blood of the תמיד!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof for its question. When an infrequent offering is ready first, does the frequent offering still go first?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the פסח was slaughtered before the תמיד, so the פסח was ready first. Even so, its blood is kept stirred and waits for the תמיד's blood to be sprinkled. That seems to show the frequent offering (תמיד) wins, even when the other one was ready earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסח offering, brought on the afternoon of the 14th of ניסן
The daily communal offering; here, the afternoon one
Stirs (the blood, so it does not clot)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rav Ashi said to Ravina:
If he slaughtered it before midday, it is disqualified,
phrases.notes: He is quoting a משנה in פסחים about the קרבן פסח.

phrases.english: because it says about it, 'in the afternoon.'
If before the daily offering, it is valid,
and someone should keep stirring its blood
until he sprinkles the blood!
phrases.notes: He means the blood of the תמיד. Stirring keeps the פסח's blood from clotting while it waits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי לְרָבִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the תפילה proof was rejected, a new proof is brought from the קרבנות themselves.
steps.raayaObject: That the frequent offering goes first even when the infrequent one was ready earlier.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in פסחים: a פסח slaughtered before the תמיד waits, with its blood stirred, until the תמיד's blood is sprinkled.

steps.title: The תמיד was already slaughtered first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof. The משנה is talking about a case where the תמיד had already been slaughtered before the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A case where he had already slaughtered the תמיד first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the פסח proof by reading the משנה as a specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תמיד was already slaughtered, then both bloods are ready for sprinkling at the same time. That is the case of 'both already slaughtered,' and there the frequent one clearly goes first. So the question about one already slaughtered and one not yet slaughtered still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (used to narrow a source to a specific case)

phrases.english: Here, what case are we dealing with?
A case where he had already slaughtered the daily offering first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 23 the same way steps 18, 20 and 22 rejected earlier proofs.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the פסחים proof, but not the question itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the תמיד was not yet slaughtered. In fact both were already slaughtered, so both were equally ready.

steps.title: The wording of the משנה supports this reading
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא סבא points out that the משנה says 'until the blood of the תמיד is sprinkled.' It does not say 'until he slaughters and sprinkles.' That shows the תמיד was already slaughtered. The גמרא accepts this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא the Elder said to רב אשי: 'The משנה is precise this way too. It teaches "until the blood of the תמיד is sprinkled," and not "until he slaughters and sprinkles the blood."' Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: A careful reading of the משנה's words backs up the rejection from the last step. The גמרא agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תמיד had not been slaughtered yet, the משנה would have needed to say 'until he slaughters and sprinkles.' Since it mentions only sprinkling, the תמיד must already have been slaughtered. So the proof from step 23 falls, and the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Is precise; its wording shows this
Learn from it (the point is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: Every proof for the frequent-versus-earlier question (the משנה of שלמים and חטאת, קידוש, תפילה, פסח) was pushed off. Each one turned out to be a case where both things were ready at the same moment.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא סָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha the Elder said to Rav Ashi:
The משנה is also precise this way,
for it teaches 'until the blood (of the daily offering) is sprinkled,'
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't. Either way, the blood meant is the תמיד's.

phrases.english: and it does not teach 'until he slaughters and sprinkles the blood.'
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rejection in step 24 from the משנה's wording.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה in פסחים is a case where the תמיד was already slaughtered.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה says only 'until the blood is sprinkled,' and leaves out 'slaughters.'

steps.title: Why may כהנים prepare the offerings any way they like?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: with all the offerings, the כהנים may eat them however they want. Then it asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And with all of them, the כהנים are permitted,' etc. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets כהנים change how they prepare קדשים, for example roasted or cooked, as they please. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק allows this.

phrases.english: 'And with all of them, the priests are permitted,' etc.
phrases.notes: Permitted to prepare and eat the offerings in whatever way they like.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the precedence question and turns to a new clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that lets כהנים prepare קדשים any way they wish.

steps.title: 'למשחה': eating like kings
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק gives the כהנים their portions 'למשחה,' which means 'for greatness.' So they may eat them the way kings eat, prepared however they like.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'למשחה,' meaning for greatness, the way kings eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'למשחה' is read as 'for greatness' or 'royalty.' Kings eat their food prepared exactly how they want. So the כהנים may do the same with their קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'for anointing'; read here as 'for greatness'

phrases.english: The verse says 'lemoshcha,'
meaning for greatness, the way kings eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'למשחה' means 'for greatness,' so כהנים eat קדשים like kings, in any style they choose.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the only oil shared out in the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. רבי שמעון says that oil being shared out among the כהנים in the עזרה can only come from two places. It is either the leftover oil from the wafers of Israelites' מנחות, or the לוג of oil of a מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי שמעון said: If you see oil being shared out in the courtyard, you don't need to ask what it is. It is the leftover from the wafers of Israelites' meal offerings, or the לוג of oil of a מצורע.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. רבי שמעון gives a rule for identifying oil that the כהנים are dividing up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון is saying that oil handed out on its own to the כהנים in the עזרה can only come from two places. One is the oil left over after the wafers of an Israelite's מנחה were smeared. The other is the rest of the מצורע's לוג after some was placed on him. So there is no need to ask where such oil came from.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with צרעת, who brings oil as part of his purification

phrases.english: MISHNA: Rabbi Shimon said:
If you saw oil
that is being shared out in the courtyard,
you don't need to ask what it is;
rather, it is the leftover of the wafers of Israelites' meal offerings,
or the log of oil of a leper.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Oil eaten by כהנים in the עזרה is only the leftover from Israelites' wafer מנחות or the מצורע's לוג of oil.

steps.title: Oil burned on the altar comes only from priests' meal offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון continues. Oil placed on the fires of the מזבח is either leftover oil from the wafers of a כהן's מנחה or oil from the מנחה of the כהן משיח, because nobody may donate oil on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you see oil being put on the fires of the altar, you don't have to ask what it is. It is either the leftover oil from the wafers of a priest's meal offering, or oil from the meal offering of the anointed priest. That is because a person may not donate oil by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues רבי שמעון's words. After explaining what oil is shared among the כהנים, he now explains what oil is burned on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן's מנחה is burned completely, so its leftover oil goes on the fire instead of to the כהנים. רבי שמעון says these are the only possible sources. Since a person may not donate oil by itself, no other kind of oil could be on the fire.

keyTerms.meaning: Thin wafers, one way a מנחה is baked
A meal offering brought by a כהן, which is burned completely
People donate something as a voluntary offering

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with Step 28. There the oil was eaten by the כהנים and came from Israelites' מנחות or a מצורע. Here the oil is burned on the מזבח and comes from offerings brought by כהנים.

phrases.english: If you saw oil
that is placed on the fires
phrases.notes: These are the fires on the מזבח.

phrases.english: you do not need to ask what it is;
rather, it is the leftover from the wafers of priests' meal offerings
or from the meal offering of the anointed priest,
because one may not donate oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם רָאִיתָ שֶׁמֶן שֶׁהוּא נִיתָּן עַל גַּבֵּי הָאִישִּׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי שמעון's statement in the משנה. Step 28 dealt with oil that is eaten, and this step deals with oil that is burned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Oil burned on the מזבח must be leftover oil from a כהן's מנחה or the מנחה of the כהן משיח, since oil cannot be donated by itself.

steps.title: רבי טרפון says oil may be donated
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון disagrees with רבי שמעון and holds that a person may donate oil by itself as an offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון says: A person may donate oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second opinion. רבי טרפון says a person may donate oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's whole list rested on the idea that oil cannot be donated by itself. רבי טרפון rejects that idea. In his view, oil on the מזבח could also be a donation, so the list of sources is no longer closed.
steps.whatToRemember: The argument is about one point: can a person donate oil by itself? רבי שמעון says no, so oil on the מזבח must come from known sources. רבי טרפון says yes.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon says:
One may donate oil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing opinion to the reason רבי שמעון gave at the end of Step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי טרפון, a person may donate oil by itself as an offering.
